title: gpui: Skip sprites whose atlas texture was released instead of panicking
body:
## Objective

Each rendering backend looked up the atlas texture for a sprite batch with an `unwrap`, so a scene referencing a texture the atlas had already released aborted the process (`metal_atlas.rs:196` in the Delta crash reports). This happens when an image is dropped while a cached view still replays a paint from before the drop — Delta hit it when re-rasterizing a zoomed Mermaid diagram.

## Solution

Texture lookups now return `Option`, and the Metal, wgpu, and DirectX sprite draws skip a batch whose texture is gone. The stale paint is replaced as soon as its view re-renders, so nothing is lost beyond that frame. wgpu also drops the cached bind group for a released texture and no longer fails the whole frame on a missing one.

This is a renderer-level safety net and is complementary to #64619, which fixes the lifetime rule in `Window` so that atlas entries are not released while a retained frame still references them. Both can land independently.

## Testing

- `corgi test -p gpui_apple metal_atlas` — 4 passed, including a new regression that the lookup reports `None` after the last tile is removed.
- `cargo test -p gpui_wgpu wgpu_atlas` — 5 passed (extended the generation test to assert `None` after removal).
- `corgi check -p gpui_wgpu`.
- DirectX changes are the same shape but have **not been compiled**; no Windows target available.

Release Notes:

- N/A
- [GPUI] Fixed a crash when an image was removed from the sprite atlas while a cached view still referenced it.
